standard_prerequisites.name: Tensoring with a module is right exact, so the sequence in question is always exact on the right
The kernel of the localization map is the submodule of elements annihilated by a power of the element, which identifies the left exactness condition

core_obligations: Record that the functor tensoring with the module is right exact, which gives exactness on the right, and that the kernel of the localization map is the submodule of elements annihilated by a power of the element, which gives the left exactness statement (proof lines 25387-25395).

Prove the forward direction of the middle exactness: if the sequence is exact in the middle, then elements of the form (x, 0) with x annihilated by a power of the element on the tensor product lie in the image of the first arrow, which says exactly that the comparison map on power torsion is surjective (proof lines 25397-25402).

Prove the converse: assume the comparison map on power torsion is surjective and take an element (x, y) of the middle mapping to zero on the right; write y as y' divided by a power of the element, use the hypothesis to write the combination as an element z annihilated by a power of the element, replace y' by y' plus z and reduce the second coordinate to the image of an element of the module (proof lines 25402-25413).

Conclude that (x, y) is the image of a single element of the module, so the sequence is exact in the middle, and read off the characterization of glueability as bijectivity of the comparison map on power torsion (proof lines 25411-25413).

Finish the two remaining statements: for a glueing pair the sequence is exact in the middle for every module, so glueability is equivalent to injectivity of the comparison map, and the statement for the completion follows from the equivalence between being a glueing pair for the pair and for its completion (proof lines 25415-25422).
proof_roadmap: Read off exactness on the right from right exactness of the tensor product and the left exactness condition from the kernel of the localization map (proof lines 25387-25395).
Prove the equivalence in the middle by an explicit element computation: one direction is immediate, the other clears denominators using the surjectivity hypothesis (proof lines 25397-25413).
Deduce the glueability criteria, using that the sequence is exact in the middle for glueing pairs, and transfer the statement from the pair to its completion (proof lines 25415-25422).
difficulty_reason: The statement characterizes the exactness of the Cech sequence of an arbitrary module for a ring map inducing isomorphisms modulo all powers of a fixed element: exactness on the right always holds, exactness on the left is equivalent to injectivity of the comparison map on power torsion, and exactness in the middle is equivalent to its surjectivity, with the resulting characterization of glueability and its specialization to glueing pairs and to the completion (statement lines 25364-25385). The proof of the middle case is an explicit element computation in which one first reduces to the torsion-free case, then treats the universal example of the ring modulo its power torsion submodule, where the Tor group vanishes by an earlier computation, and finally passes to a general module through a free presentation whose sequence remains exact after tensoring because of the completion statement (proof lines 25387-25423). The reduction to the universal case and the presentation step are the substantive moves.
